name: OSQ (Operating Systems Questions)
description: OSQ (Operating Systems Questions) is a real-world, expert-graded benchmark for Automated Subjective Answer Evaluation (ASAE). It contains 138 hand-transcribed,expert-graded responses from 23 second-year Computer Science Engineering students, collected during a routine mid-semester Operating Systems examination at Sardar Patel Institute of Technology (SPIT), Mumbai, India. From an original cohort of 83 students, 23 scripts were purposively sampled to span the full range of performance, writing, style, and expression. Each answer script was scanned, manually transcribed (OCR followed by human proof-reading), and graded against a component-level synoptic rubric by a domainexpert, yielding subpart-level human ground truth across four heterogeneous question types: (i) true/false-with-reason, (ii) choose-one-with-reason, (iii) short code/query,and (iv) Gantt-chart long-form scheduling answers (with decomposed sub-fields for the schedule table, charts, CPU utilisation, and average turnaround/waiting time). Thismulti-format, rubric-aligned structure makes OSQ suitable for benchmarking partial-credit-aware, question-type-aware grading systems that a single-format corpus cannotsupport.
